text: @skornblith @thao_nguyen26 @maithra_raghu Awesome work, congrats! BTW, a similar block structure exists in transformer GMs (like iGPT) too! I had hoped that concatenating representations from different blocks would help me beat SimCLR 🙃, but turns out it wasn't much better than the best single layer.

author: markchen90
text: A pure transformer on sequences of image patches outperforms SOTA CNN classifiers, while using fewer parameters and less compute. One of the top ICLR submissions this year! Thanks @hendrycks for the share.

quoted.text:
An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale 

When pre-trained and transferred to CV tasks, Vision Transformer attains excellent results compared to SOTA CNNs while requiring much fewer computational resources to train.

https://t.co/8rPsmMfucx https://t.co/WdoIM0E28Y

author: markchen90
text: Also, congrats to William Lin for becoming the new IOI champion. That's 3 years in a row now where the top spot belongs to the USA!

author: markchen90
text: The first online IOI just concluded (preliminary rankings here: https://t.co/51r2b14aRt). So much effort went into ensuring the contest could happen, and our students worked just as hard to prepare. Congrats to Team USA for 3 golds and 1 silver!

author: markchen90
text: Great post! An AR model on any image dataset assigns absurdly high logp to a blank image, even though it looks nothing like train images. Less surprising once you consider that the zero vector is the max likelihood sample from a multivariate Gaussian (but not in its typical set).

quoted.text:
New blog post, in which I wax lyrical about typicality and the curse of dimensionality: https://t.co/JrRUB83Pcr

I tweeted about this concept a while back, but it turns out I have more to say on the topic. It's a bit more speculative than what I usually write, hope you like it!

author: markchen90
text: @PreetumNakkiran @heghbalz @karpathy At GPT-1 scale, the error with just CIFAR-10 pretraining was 1.5-2 times the error with ImageNet pretraining.

author: markchen90
text: @PreetumNakkiran Likely so! @rewonfc's Sparse Transformer was partly motivated by strided and local attention patterns (with stride/length equal to the image sidelength) that naturally emerged when training dense image transformers.

text: @anh_ng8 @AlecRad @rewonfc @ilyasut Thanks for the kind words! Yes, these images are almost certainly in the training set and memorized. We made sure to check that log likelihood for an example did not change significantly after an optimizer update.
